Tom Carter ran well to finish 2nd, and George Hoath was 3rd. With Len Herbert 6th and Tom Morrell 8th we scored an easy win in the team championship, an honour which we have secured in 1925, 1926, 1929, 1930, 1931, 1933, 1934, 1935, 1936 and 1937.

Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear.

The field was led out by Tom Carter but was well together when at 2 miles Carter went into the lead. Tom's lead, however, was doomed as his injured leg gave way immediately and he had to retire from the race.

In 1932 young HARRY SHIELDS won the Middlesex Junior Cross-country Championship; and in 1933 the Club Championship at 7 miles had in its leading positions PENNY, ALLUM, CARTER; and a Belgrave v Cadogan match, in conjunction, gave Belgrave a 38 to 40 points win, six aside scoring.
